meeting_header:
Date: 2026-04-30
Time: 15:00 - 16:02 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: available
Attendees: Sofia Martin (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Ava Gomez (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (LynxBridge Head of ML), Dan O'Leary (LynxBridge Platform), Marco Ruiz (LynxBridge Product)
summary: Kickoff for onboarding sprint. Covered pilot goals, security/compliance checklist, networking/VPC requirements, pilot dataset and success metrics, timeline to initial POC, and next steps for runbook and pricing. Customer leaned toward Dedicated for p99 guarantees but open to hybrid pilot. Action items assigned.
topics: Introductions; Goals & success criteria; Security and compliance (SOC2, SSO, KMS, retention); Network & VPC peering; Model choice / quantization; Throughput & latency targets; Rollout plan and canary strategy; Next steps and owner commitments
transcript:
00:00 Sofia: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Sofia from Redwood, im the AE on this engagement um Marcus our SE will cover the technical plan, Ava from CSM to help with the runbook.
00:14 Priya: hi thanks, excited to get started. we have a few stakeholders outside but this core team will run the pilot.
00:25 Marcus: great quick agenda - clarify success metrics, map network steps, agree pilot model and capacity, then timeline. sound good?
00:36 Marco: yes also wanna make sure product metrics are captured - hallucination tolerance, latency under load.
00:46 Dan: just to flag we need VPC peering and we have fairly tight egress rules, our infra team might need an hour with your network engineer.
00:58 Sofia: noted we usually do a network handshake and provide a checklist. i'll send that after the call.
01:08 Marcus: can i ask about expected qps and p99 targets? that will drive Dedicated sizing vs hosted.
01:18 Priya: for the initial pilot we expect around 30 qps with p50 < 150ms and p99 < 600ms, but that last is flexible if cost is too high.
01:30 Marcus: okay 30 qps with p99 600ms is doable on a modest Dedicated pool with some autoscaling. we can also try hosted with routing to cheaper variants but for consistent p99 you typically land on Dedicated or pinned hosts.
01:47 Priya: what's the tradeoff again between Dedicated and hosted?
01:51 Marcus: hosted is simpler and cheaper at low volume but lacks isolation and tight latency SLOs. Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools, predictable latencies and better control over caching and KV cache reuse. it costs more but reduces variance.
02:09 Dan: security question - we need KMS integration and support for our HSM, plus audit logs retained for 12 months.
02:18 Ava: we have KMS integrations and can map to customer KMS; audit logs and extended retention are an add-on, i'll include details in the security pack.
02:29 Marco: also SSO - SAML ok? we use Okta.
02:34 Sofia: yes SAML/SSO via Okta is standard, we'll include the SAML metadata.
02:40 Priya: on model side we're leaning open-models cost conscious. we also need quantization for cost savings but worried about accuracy regressions.
02:52 Marcus: we do model recommendations by workload - for retrieval-augmented generation we often recommend a 7b quantized variant with evals on your prompts. we can run a head-to-head on a small eval set to measure delta.
03:07 Priya: perfect, we'll share prompt set. expectation is no more than 2% accuracy drop vs baseline.
03:15 Marcus: noted. also will instrument quality monitors - Redwood Optimize can watch model drift and surface regressions tied to prompt sets.
03:26 Dan: on networking, is VPC peering mandatory for Dedicated? any VPN option?
03:33 Marcus: we support VPC peering and private link depending on region, and also a site-to-site VPN option for on-prem. peering is preferred for throughput.
03:44 Dan: ok we'll prioritize peering.
03:47 Sofia: timeline thoughts - propose 2-week prep (network + security), 2-week pilot run, then decision. so about 6 weeks total including contract. Thoughts?
03:58 Priya: that aligns with our Q2 goals.
04:02 Marco: who owns the contract loop if concessions needed?
04:06 Sofia: i'll handle initial terms and pricing, legal can loop in later - but i'll include a pilot-friendly clause.
04:12 Marcus: technical POC outline - step 1 env provisioning (dedicated pool or hosted routing), step 2 ingest test dataset + KV caching config, step 3 run load and quality evals, step 4 iterate quantization/latency knobs.
04:31 Priya: on KV cache - does Redwood support prefix caching for conversation histories?
04:37 Marcus: yes, prefix and selective KV caching. that helps p99 and reduces generation cost. we'll show config examples.
04:46 Dan: do you have observability hooks to our telemetry stack? we use Datadog and internal tracing.
04:52 Ava: yes we have tracing hooks and token-level cost metrics, can export to Datadog or S3. i'll add the observability doc link.
05:05 Marco: question on fallbacks - if Dedicated saturated, will requests route to a cheaper fallback model?
05:12 Marcus: yes we can configure smart routing policies for cost vs latency tradeoffs; model variants must be validated first to prevent quality regressions.
05:23 Priya: ok good. also we need to confirm compliance posture - do you have SOC2 Type II?
05:29 Sofia: we are SOC2 Type II compliant, and we'll attach the cert in the security pack.
05:35 Dan: retention - can we enforce data deletion after 30 days for pilot?
05:40 Ava: yes retention policies can be configured per workspace; we'll document the default and the short retention option.
05:49 Marcus: one more tech note - for your retrieval stack, if you want low-latency 100ms p50, we may recommend local embedding cache + a smaller model for short queries.
06:00 Priya: makes sense. we'll include RAG details in the prompt set.
06:07 Sofia: Recap - action owners and dates as discussed. i'll send the onboarding runbook + security pack today, Marcus will propose the POC scope by Monday, Dan to schedule network handshake, Priya to share workload and prompts.
06:20 Marco: sounds good thanks everyone.
06:24 Sofia: thanks all we'll follow up, meeting adjourned.
questions: Can Redwood integrate with customer HSM/KMS? - Answer: Yes, KMS integrations available; details in security pack.
Is VPC peering mandatory for Dedicated? - Answer: Preferred but VPN supported; details depend on region.
What are typical p99 latencies for a 7b quantized model? - Answer: We'll provide benchmark sheet; expect 200-700ms depending on batch and cache.
